svg.title: Humanoid robot – power diagram
svg.desc: Power wiring: 4S 18650 pack with 4S 20 A BMS, 20 A fuse, XT60 and main switch, then a servo branch (SERVO E-STOP, 6 V buck, 1000 uF, distribution, PCA9685 V+), a Pi branch (5.1 V buck, 470 uF, Pi pins 2/4 and 5 V loads) and a battery-sense divider to MCP3008 CH1. Charger port to the BMS.

g.text: Sheet 2 of 2 · 4S Li-ion pack → 20 A fuse → XT60 + main switch → servo, Pi and battery-sense branches · every ground is joined
Signals: wiring_diagram.svg · steps and checklist: WIRING.md
14.8 V nominal · 16.8 V full · 13.2 V low
cell protection + balancing; P+ = pack + (straight through)
load and charger both use P− / P+
charge with the main switch OFF
the robot will go limp / fall
(≈ 15 A if it were at 6 V)
6 × MG996R can pull ≈ 15 A together at stall: keep the 6 V and its ground short and thick.
If your PCA9685 board has thin V+ traces, take the servo red/brown wires from the
distribution board and plug only the orange signal wires into the PCA9685.
Software stop as well: GPIO22 drives PCA9685 OE HIGH = all servo pulses off.
Powering the Pi 3B through pins 2/4 bypasses its input protection: set the buck to
5.10 V first, and NEVER plug in micro-USB at the same time.
thin wire (22 AWG) — a few µA only
COMMON GROUND BUS — battery P−, both bucks, servos, Pi GND pins, sense divider
A 4S 18650 pack must be built or checked by a qualified person.
Use 4 matched cells (same model, capacity and state of charge), a 4S BMS
and a 16.8 V 4S charger. Never solder directly to cells without spot-welded
tabs, never charge unattended, and keep the pack away from metal parts.
A shorted pack can deliver more than 50 A — that is what the fuse is for.
Do not mix this 4S design with the older 2S2P charger or BMS.
pack, fuse, XT60, main switch, SERVO E-STOP, 6 V buck in/out,
servo distribution, servo grounds, ground bus near the bucks
5.1 V buck in/out → Pi pins 2/4 and 6/14, charger port
signals, balance leads, battery sense, small 5 V loads
White pill on a wire = wire gauge. Dot = joined.
Set the 6 V and 5.1 V bucks with a meter BEFORE anything is connected.
Power the Pi alone first, then add the parts one at a time (WIRING.md).
⚠ COMMON GROUND required • NEVER power servos from the Pi • Pi GPIO is 3.3 V ONLY
The SERVO E-STOP only removes servo power — the Pi keeps running. Turn the main switch OFF before changing any wiring.
